# [CS033] Session Cookie Without HttpOnly (cookie-missing-httponly)

A session cookie is readable by JavaScript.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-1004](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1004.html) |
| **OWASP** | A07:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Without HttpOnly, any XSS on the site can read the session cookie and send it to an attacker.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{Name: "session", Value: id, Secure: true})
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{Name: "session", Value: id, Secure: true, HttpOnly: true, SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode})
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [cookie-missing-httponly]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    cookie-missing-httponly: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore cookie-missing-httponly -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** cookie-missing-httponly
```
